records.question: How many credits do I need to take to be full-time as a graduate student?
search_queries: How many credits do I need to take to be full-time as a graduate student?
records.answer:
As a graduate student on F-1 or J-1 status, you need at least **9 credits per term** to be full-time.

Conditions that affect what counts:

- **Online courses:** No more than **3 credits** of online or distance coursework can count toward full-time enrollment each term. So at least **6 of your 9 credits** must be face-to-face or hybrid. ISSS has said that hybrid classes count as in-person for immigration purposes.
- **Audited courses** don't count toward the minimum.
- **Dropping below 9 credits:** Don't drop or withdraw from a course mid-term without approval from an ISSS advisor. Taking fewer credits requires written [Less Than Full Time (LTFT)](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/less-than-full-time) authorization from ISSS. You must get it *before* you drop below full-time. Requests are due by the add/drop deadline, or at the latest before the withdrawal deadline (Friday of week 7). Graduate students approved for LTFT for academic reasons must still take at least **4.5 credits**.

If you're unsure whether a particular course schedule meets the requirement, it's best to confirm with an ISSS advisor.

Sources: [Maintaining F-1 and J-1 Student Status](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/f-1-j-1-maintain), [Less Than Full Time](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/less-than-full-time), [Termination of SEVP COVID-19 Flexibilities (2023)](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2023/June/termination-of-sevp-covid-19-flexibilities)

records.question: How many hours a week can I work on campus while classes are in session?
search_queries: How many hours a week can I work on campus while classes are in session?
records.answer:
**Up to 20 hours per week** while school is in session. That's the limit for both F-1 and J-1 students.

**Key conditions:**
- **Breaks:** You can work more than 20 hours per week during an approved vacation term. Check with Drexel's Office of Human Resources about their own (non-immigration) policies for this.
- **Co-op:** During a co-op cycle, your co-op counts as your "class," so on-campus work is still capped at 20 hours per week. ISSS strongly discourages doing both at the same time.
- **Eligibility:** You must be a continuing student maintaining valid F-1/J-1 status at Drexel. You must not have graduated, and your I-20/DS-2019 must not have expired.
- **J-1 students:** You need prior ISSS authorization for any on-campus job.
- **Over 20 hours for your program:** If your curriculum requires more than 20 hours per week of on-campus work, F-1 students must apply for CPT.
- **Academics come first:** Work must not hurt your academic performance or full-time enrollment.

Sources: [On-Campus Employment](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/on-campus-employment), [Maintaining F-1 and J-1 Student Status](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/f-1-j-1-maintain), [CPT](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/cpt)

records.question: How long is the grace period after I finish my program on an F-1 visa?
search_queries: How long is the grace period after I finish my program on an F-1 visa?
records.answer:
**According to the ISSS website, F-1 students and their dependents currently have a 60-day grace period after their program ends.** [Maintaining F-1 and J-1 Student Status](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/f-1-j-1-maintain)

**During the grace period you may:**
- Pack and prepare to leave the U.S.
- Travel within the U.S.
- Apply for OPT, transfer to a new school, start a new program, or change status.

**You may not** work or study. If you leave the U.S. during the grace period, you can't re-enter in F-1 status after your I-20 end date.

**If you apply for OPT:** As long as USCIS receives your application before the 60 days end, you can stay in the U.S. while it's pending. When your OPT later ends, you get another 60-day grace period, but not if you went over the 90-day unemployment limit. [OPT](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/opt)

**Possible change:** A 2025 ISSS announcement said a DHS proposal to replace Duration of Status would cut the F-1 grace period to 30 days. On July 17, 2026, ISSS reported that DHS published a final rule eliminating Duration of Status. On September 14, 2026, ISSS reported that a U.S. District Court postponed that rule's effective date. The excerpts I have don't say what the final rule says about the grace period. Check the [September 2026 announcement](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2026/September/US-District-Court-Postpones-Effective-Date-of-DHS-Final-Rule-on-Duration-of-Status), and confirm with an ISSS advisor before you plan your departure or next steps.

records.question: How much OPT can I get?
search_queries: How much OPT can I get?
records.answer:
**Standard OPT:** F-1 students get **12 months of OPT per degree level** (Bachelor's, Master's, Doctorate). You can use it in two ways:
- **Pre-Completion OPT** (during your program):
  - Part-time counts at 50%. For example, 6 months part-time uses 3 months of your 12.
  - Full-time counts at 100%. For example, 6 months full-time uses 6 months.
- **Post-Completion OPT** (after graduation): you can save all 12 months for this.

**STEM OPT Extension:** If your degree is in a qualifying STEM field, you may be eligible for an **additional 24 months** after your Post-Completion OPT. You can't request all 36 months at once. First you apply for the initial 12 months of Post-Completion OPT. Then you apply for the STEM extension while your OPT EAD card is still active. STEM OPT employers must use E-Verify, and the job must be directly related to your STEM degree.

**Recent news:** On October 9, 2026, ISSS announced a DHS *proposed* rule. It would require universities to pay a $70,000 fee for each student's OPT and $30,000 for STEM OPT. ISSS says this has **no immediate impact**, and current OPT and STEM OPT processes are unchanged unless a final rule is published and put into effect.

Sources: [OPT](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/opt) · [STEM OPT Extension](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/stem-opt-extension) · [DHS Fee Announcement](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2026/October/Department-of-Homeland-Security-Proposes-$70000-Fee-for-OPT-and-$30000-fee-for-STEM-OPT)

records.question: How many days can I be unemployed on post-completion OPT?
search_queries: How many days can I be unemployed on post-completion OPT?
records.answer:
**You can have up to 90 days of unemployment in total on Post-Completion OPT.**

**How the days are counted**
- Every day without qualifying employment counts, **including weekends**.
- The count starts on the employment start date on your EAD card.
- Qualifying employment means **at least 20 hours per week**. Remote work counts if it meets this minimum.

**If you get the STEM OPT Extension**
- You get an **additional 60 days**, for a **maximum of 150 days** across the initial 12 months and the 24-month extension combined.
- If you lose or leave a job during STEM OPT, you must report to ISSS and submit a final Form I-983 evaluation within 10 days.

**If you go over the limit**
- Exceeding the limit is a violation of F-1 status. Your SEVIS record may be terminated, and it can affect future benefits like an H-1B or green card.
- You also lose the 60-day grace period after OPT.
- Before you reach the limit, you should prepare to change educational level or transfer schools, leave the U.S., or take other action to maintain status.
- You must report any loss or interruption of employment to ISSS.

If you're getting close to the limit, talk with your ISSS advisor about your options.

Sources: [Optional Practical Training (OPT)](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/opt) · [STEM OPT Extension](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/stem-opt-extension)

records.question: Do I need a job offer to apply for OPT?
search_queries: Do I need a job offer to apply for OPT?
records.answer:
**No, you don't need a job offer to apply for OPT.** This applies to both Pre-Completion and Post-Completion OPT. ([OPT page](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/opt))

**What to keep in mind:**

- **Post-Completion OPT:** You're expected to actively look for work in your field of study. You can have **no more than 90 days of unemployment in total**. Every day without qualifying employment counts, including weekends, starting from the start date on your EAD. If you're nearing that limit, plan ahead. Your options include transferring schools, changing your educational level, leaving the U.S., or taking other steps to maintain status.
- **Pre-Completion OPT:** There's no penalty for not working. However, any time you use comes out of your 12 months of OPT eligibility.
- **Before you start any job:** Wait until you have your EAD card *and* its start date has arrived.

**STEM OPT is different.** The 24-month STEM extension *does* require a job or job offer. It must be related to your STEM degree and come from an employer enrolled in E-Verify. ([STEM OPT page](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/stem-opt-extension))

**Recent news:** On October 9, 2026, ISSS posted an announcement that DHS has *proposed* new fees for OPT and STEM OPT. This is a proposal, and I don't have details on its status. See the [announcement](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2026/October/Department-of-Homeland-Security-Proposes-$70000-Fee-for-OPT-and-$30000-fee-for-STEM-OPT) and check with ISSS if you're planning to apply soon.

records.question: Can I be self-employed during the STEM OPT extension?
search_queries: Can I be self-employed during the STEM OPT extension?
records.answer:
**No.** Self-employment can't be the basis for a STEM OPT extension. The regulations require a **bona fide employer-employee relationship** with an employer. ([STEM OPT Extension](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/stem-opt-extension))

**What is allowed:**
- You can work for a **start-up business**, as long as all regulatory requirements are met. You **can't sign the employer attestations on your own behalf**.
- Your STEM OPT employer must:
  - have an EIN
  - be enrolled in and using **E-Verify** at your worksite
  - offer a job directly related to your STEM degree
- You can work for multiple employers only if you work **at least 20 hours per week for each one**, and each employer meets all of the criteria above.

**How this differs from regular OPT:** During your initial 12-month Post-Completion OPT, self-employment *is* allowed. You must work full-time, hold the proper business licenses, and run a business related to your degree. That option ends once you move to the STEM extension. ([OPT](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/opt))

**Also worth knowing:** On October 9, 2026, ISSS posted that DHS has [proposed a $30,000 fee for STEM OPT](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2026/October/Department-of-Homeland-Security-Proposes-$70000-Fee-for-OPT-and-$30000-fee-for-STEM-OPT). This is a proposal, not a current rule.

For your specific situation, such as a business you own or co-founded, please confirm with an ISSS advisor.

records.question: Does my employer need to use E-Verify for my STEM OPT?
search_queries: Does my employer need to use E-Verify for my STEM OPT?
records.answer:

**Other employer requirements:**
- The employer must have an Employment Identification Number (EIN).
- The job must be directly related to your qualifying STEM degree.
- There must be a real employer-employee relationship, so self-employment and staffing or temporary agencies likely won't qualify.
- If you work for more than one employer at the same time, **each** must meet these rules (including E-Verify), and you must work at least 20 hours per week for each.

**The E-Verify number on your forms:**
- You'll enter your employer's E-Verify number on the [STEM OPT Request Form](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/~/media/Drexel/EMSS-Site-Group/StudentLife/Documents/international-student-support/forms/stem-opt-request.pdf).
- If you change employers later, the [STEM OPT Employment Update Form](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/~/media/Drexel/EMSS-Site-Group/StudentLife/Documents/international-student-support/forms/stem-opt-employment.pdf) asks for the new employer's number. You must report the change to ISSS within 10 days.
- If you don't know the number, ask your supervisor or your company's HR department.

If you're unsure whether a specific job qualifies, confirm with an ISSS advisor.

records.question: How recent does the travel signature on my I-20 need to be when I come back to the U.S.?
search_queries: How recent does the travel signature on my I-20 need to be when I come back to the U.S.?
records.answer:
**It depends on your status, and ISSS pages differ, so the safest approach is to have a signature no older than 6 months when you re-enter.**

- **F-1 students (currently studying):** The [Travel Information](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/travel) page says the travel signature must be issued **within 12 months** of re-entry. However, the [Visa Renewal](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/visa-renewal) page says to request a new signature if yours will be **more than six months old** when you return. Because of this difference, aim for 6 months and confirm with ISSS.
- **F-1 on Post-Completion OPT or STEM OPT:** The signature may be **no older than 6 months**. The [Travel Information](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/travel), [OPT](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/opt), and [STEM OPT Extension](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/stem-opt-extension) pages all agree on this.

**Need a new signature?** A December 2024 ISSS announcement pointed students to the [Signature Request form](https://drexel.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_6KHlTvO1gmy8Sfs). Since that announcement is older, check with ISSS that it's still the current process. Request it well before you travel.

records.question: How much extra money do I need to show to bring my spouse and one child?

records.question: How long does USCIS take to process an OPT application?

records.answer:

**Timing tips from ISSS:**
- **Post-completion OPT:** You can apply as early as 90 days before your program end date and no later than 60 days after it. Apply well before the deadline. If USCIS doesn't receive your application within the 60-day grace period, it will be denied.
- **Pre-completion OPT:** You can apply up to 90 days before your requested start date. ISSS suggests choosing a start date earlier than your planned employment date to allow for delays.
- Before you file with USCIS, ISSS needs about 4–5 business days to issue your OPT I-20. You must then file Form I-765 within 30 days of that recommendation.
- You can't start working until you receive your EAD.

That information is over three years old, so the fee or timeframe may have changed.

**Recent news:** On October 9, 2026, ISSS posted that [DHS proposes a $70,000 fee for OPT](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2026/October/Department-of-Homeland-Security-Proposes-$70000-Fee-for-OPT-and-$30000-fee-for-STEM-OPT). records.question: How long can a J-1 master's student do Academic Training?
search_queries: How long can a J-1 master's student do Academic Training?
records.answer:
A J-1 master's student can do **up to 18 months of Academic Training (AT), or the length of the degree program, whichever is shorter.** Students in a STEM degree may qualify for a special extension.

**How the time is counted:**
- AT during your studies and AT after your program ends are added together toward the limit.
- Full-time and part-time AT count the same.
- Total AT can't exceed the length of your academic program.

**Key conditions:**
- Your DS-2019 must be issued by Drexel, not an outside agency such as Fulbright.
- You must be in good academic standing.
- The training must relate directly to the major on your DS-2019.
- AT must be approved and listed on your DS-2019 before your program end date.
- AT must start no later than 30 days after your program ends.
- Submit the Academic Training form through the [ISSS Student Portal](https://drexel0.sharepoint.com/sites/ISSS-StudentPortal/SitePages/ISSS-Student-Forms.aspx) at least 30 days before your DS-2019 end date. ISSS recommends 3 weeks or more in advance.

**Upcoming change to watch:** In July 2026, DHS published a [final rule eliminating Duration of Status](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2026/July/Department-of-Homeland-Security-Publishes-Final-Rule-Eliminating-Duration-of-Status). It was scheduled to take effect September 15, 2026. A September 14 ISSS announcement says a court [postponed that effective date](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2026/September/US-District-Court-Postpones-Effective-Date-of-DHS-Final-Rule-on-Duration-of-Status). If the rule takes effect, post-graduation AT may require an extension of stay from USCIS. Please confirm the current status with an ISSS advisor.

records.question: What happens if I'm away from Drexel and not enrolled for more than five months?
search_queries: What happens if I'm away from Drexel and not enrolled for more than five months?
records.answer:
If you're not enrolled for **more than five (5) months**, you'll need a **new I-20/DS-2019** to return, and you'll have to **pay the SEVIS I-901 fee again**. ([Vacation and Leave of Absence](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/vacation-loa))

**What this means:**
- **It's a break in your F-1 status.** After you return, you must complete **at least one academic year of full-time study** before you're eligible for certain F-1 benefits, such as **CPT or OPT**.
- **The same applies to some shorter absences.** You also need a new I-20/DS-2019 if your SEVIS record was terminated for any reason other than "Authorized Early Withdrawal."

**Steps to return:**
1. **Get approval from your academic program.** Your academic advisor will explain how to report your return to Drexel.
2. **Email ISSS at least three (3) months before your planned return** for instructions on applying for the new I-20/DS-2019.

**For comparison:** If ISSS authorized your absence and your break is **less than five months**, you may be able to have your SEVIS record reactivated instead. You'd submit documents 1–2 months before returning. SEVP decides these requests at its discretion.

Also, contact ISSS **before** you leave or take a leave of absence. ([Current Students](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students))

For your own situation, it's best to confirm the details with an ISSS advisor.

records.question: How old can my bank statement be for my I-20 application?

records.question: How do I get a Social Security Number for my on-campus job?
search_queries: How do I get a Social Security Number for my on-campus job?
records.answer:
You can apply for an SSN once you have a **paid on-campus job**. Here are the steps from ISSS:

1. **Register your I-20/DS-2019 first.** Complete the *F-1 ISSS Mandatory Immigration Modules & I-20 Registration* or the *J-1 DS-2019 Registration*. New students should then wait about **8–10 business days** before applying.
2. **Follow the "SSN Instructions"** in the [ISSS Student Portal](https://drexel0.sharepoint.com/sites/ISSS-StudentPortal/SitePages/ISSS-Student-Forms.aspx).
3. **Request an SSN support letter** by emailing your job offer letter to isss@drexel.edu. The letter must include:
   - your name
   - your employer's name and contact information
   - your job position
   - your hours per week
   - your employment start date
4. **Fill out Form SS-5 online** (recommended). ISSS points to the Social Security Administration for this: [Form SS-5 online](https://www.ssa.gov/number-card) (external).
5. **Finish in person.** Schedule an appointment or walk in to an SSA office to show your documents. You can find one with the [SSA office locator](https://secure.ssa.gov/ICON/main.jsp) (external).

Notes:
- If you already have an SSN from an earlier status or stay in the U.S., you can't get a new one. SSNs don't expire.
- **J-1 students** must get ISSS permission before starting any on-campus job. To do this, email your job offer to isss@drexel.edu.
- Having an SSN does not by itself authorize you to work.

records.question: How do I transfer my SEVIS record to another university?

records.question: How do I apply for a reduced course load for medical reasons?
search_queries: How do I apply for a reduced course load for medical reasons?
records.answer:
You can apply for a medical reduced course load (less than full time, or LTFT) through ISSS. You must get ISSS approval before you drop below full time.

**Steps:**
1. **Get a letter from your medical provider.** It must be on official letterhead and signed by a licensed medical doctor, doctor of osteopathy, or licensed clinical psychologist. It should say you can't attend classes full time, or can't take any classes, for a specific term. Your doctor should use ISSS's suggested template. They don't have to give your diagnosis, but the letter must include everything the template asks for.
2. **Complete the Less Than Full-Time form** on the [ISSS Student Portal](https://drexel0.sharepoint.com/sites/ISSS-StudentPortal/SitePages/ISSS-Student-Forms.aspx?source=https%3a%2f%2fdrexel0.sharepoint.com%2fsites%2fISSS-StudentPortal%2fSitePages%2fForms%2fByAuthor.aspx). Your academic advisor must give the reason and sign it.
3. **Email the form and the doctor's letter as one PDF** to isss@drexel.edu, by the add/drop deadline or at the latest before the withdrawal deadline (Friday of week 7).
4. **Wait for ISSS's email decision** before dropping any classes.

**Key conditions:**
- You can have up to 12 total months of medical LTFT per program level.
- Approval is needed for each term separately.
- You're expected to return to full-time study afterward.
- In your final term, you must still take at least one course.

records.question: What do I have to submit every six months while on STEM OPT?
search_queries: What do I have to submit every six months while on STEM OPT?
records.answer:

records.question: What's the difference between CPT and OPT?
search_queries: What's the difference between CPT and OPT?
records.answer:
**CPT** is work authorization tied to your curriculum, and ISSS approves it. **OPT** is work experience related to your degree, and USCIS approves it.

**Curricular Practical Training (CPT)**
- It is only for an internship, co-op, practicum, or other training that is a **required part of your academic program** for all students in it.
- Wanting useful or relevant work experience isn't enough to qualify.
- ISSS authorizes it, term by term, based on the Drexel academic calendar. Steinbright co-ops follow the co-op cycle dates.
- **Important:** 364 days or more of *full-time* CPT eliminates OPT eligibility. Part-time CPT doesn't affect it.
- [CPT page](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/cpt)

**Optional Practical Training (OPT)**
- It is temporary employment directly related to your major. You can use it when CPT isn't an option or after graduation.
- It is available before completing your studies (Pre-Completion) or after (Post-Completion).
- **USCIS** decides, and processing can take 90 days or more.
- To be eligible, you need at least one full academic year of full-time enrollment in the U.S., lawful F-1 status, and fewer than 365 days of full-time CPT.
- A job offer isn't required. However, on Post-Completion OPT you're expected to be employed within 9 months of your start date.
- [OPT page](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/opt)

**Note:** On October 9, 2026, ISSS posted that DHS has *proposed* a new OPT fee: [announcement](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2026/October/Department-of-Homeland-Security-Proposes-$70000-Fee-for-OPT-and-$30000-fee-for-STEM-OPT). This is a proposal, not a final rule.

For your specific situation, please confirm with an ISSS advisor.

records.question: Will doing CPT affect my OPT eligibility?
search_queries: Will doing CPT affect my OPT eligibility?
records.answer:
**Only if you use a full year or more of full-time CPT.** Part-time CPT doesn't affect OPT eligibility.

- **Full-time CPT:** Using one year or more of full-time CPT at your current degree level eliminates your OPT eligibility. The OPT page says you must have **fewer than 365 days** of full-time CPT. Exceeding this limit is one of the common reasons OPT applications are denied.
- **Part-time CPT (20 hours/week or less) and international co-op:** These don't affect OPT eligibility.
- **Degree level:** The limit applies to your current educational level.

If you're close to the limit, ask an ISSS advisor to confirm your total before accepting more full-time CPT. You can find their contact details on the [ISSS website](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support).

records.question: Can I work an on-campus job while I'm on co-op?
search_queries: Can I work an on-campus job while I'm on co-op?
records.answer:
**Yes, it's technically allowed, but ISSS strongly discourages it.**

According to the [On-Campus Employment](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/on-campus-employment) page:

- **20-hour limit:** During your co-op cycle, your co-op job counts as your "class." That means on-campus work is limited to **20 hours per week**, the same as when school is in session.
- **Co-op comes first:** Your on-campus job must not affect your ability to do your co-op job.
- **Valid status required:** You must be maintaining valid F-1/J-1 status, have an unexpired I-20/DS-2019, and not have graduated.

**Extra steps depending on your status:**
- **J-1 students:** You must get ISSS permission *before* accepting any on-campus job. Email isss@drexel.edu with your job offer, including the position title and expected start and end dates.
- **F-1 students:** You don't need advance ISSS approval. You'll still complete onboarding and the I-9 process with Drexel HR. See HR's [Student Employee and Work Study Hiring Guide](https://drexel.edu/hr/management/staffing/duhiringguides/dustudent) (external to ISSS).

Since ISSS discourages combining the two, it's a good idea to talk with an ISSS advisor before you commit. You can find contact details at [ISSS](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support).

records.question: Tôi có thể làm CPT trong năm học đầu tiên không?
search_queries: Tôi có thể làm CPT trong năm học đầu tiên không?
records.answer:
**Thông thường là không.** Theo trang CPT của ISSS, bạn chỉ đủ điều kiện CPT sau khi đã **học toàn thời gian hợp pháp trong một chương trình cấp bằng và có mặt tại Mỹ ít nhất một năm học đầy đủ** (3 quý hoặc 2 học kỳ).

**Ngoại lệ:** Sinh viên **sau đại học (graduate)** có chương trình **yêu cầu tham gia CPT ngay từ đầu** có thể được làm CPT sớm hơn.

Ngoài ra, CPT phải là phần **bắt buộc đối với tất cả sinh viên** trong chương trình, liên quan trực tiếp đến ngành học, và bạn cần có lời mời thực tập hoặc đào tạo.

**Các trường hợp có thể không cần CPT trong năm đầu:**
- **Làm việc trong khuôn viên Drexel** tối đa 20 giờ/tuần không cần CPT (xem [On-Campus Employment](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/on-campus-employment)).
- **Co-op quốc tế** hoặc đào tạo diễn ra hoàn toàn ngoài nước Mỹ không cần CPT. Tuy nhiên, bạn **không được làm việc từ xa khi đang ở Mỹ** nếu không có giấy phép lao động, dù nhà tuyển dụng ở đâu.

Nếu bạn là sinh viên sau đại học và nghĩ chương trình của mình thuộc diện ngoại lệ, hãy hỏi cố vấn học tập (hoặc cố vấn co-op tại Steinbright) và xác nhận với cố vấn ISSS trước khi bắt đầu làm việc.

records.question: OPT申请需要多长时间？
search_queries: OPT申请需要多长时间？
records.answer:
**简短回答：** 根据ISSS网站，USCIS审理OPT申请**可能需要90天或更长时间**。

**大致流程和时间：**
1. **ISSS签发OPT I-20：** ISSS收到完整申请后约 **4–5个工作日**。
2. **向USCIS递交I-765：** 必须在OPT推荐（I-20）签发后 **30天内**提交。
3. **USCIS审理：** 通常 **90天或更久**。最新处理时间可查看 [USCIS案件处理时间页面](https://egov.uscis.gov/processing-times)（外部链接）。
4. **收据通知（Receipt Notice）：** USCIS收到申请后约 **2–3周**寄出。

**申请时间窗口：**
- **毕业后OPT：** 最早可在项目结束日前90天申请，最晚在毕业后60天宽限期结束前申请。建议尽早递交，因为USCIS若在宽限期结束后才收到申请，申请会被拒。
- **毕业前OPT：** 最早可在希望开始日期前90天申请。

**加急处理：** ISSS在 **2023年3月**的公告中提到，USCIS可为OPT申请提供I-907加急处理，当时费用为$1,500，处理时间为30个日历日。这是较早的信息，现行费用和政策请向ISSS确认。

另外请注意，ISSS于2026年10月9日发布公告，称DHS**提议**对OPT收取新费用（[公告链接](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2026/October/Department-of-Homeland-Security-Proposes-$70000-Fee-for-OPT-and-$30000-fee-for-STEM-OPT)）。这目前只是提议，具体情况请关注ISSS后续通知。

- passaporte válido por mais de seis meses após a data de retorno

records.question: Do I pay the SEVIS I-901 fee again after a long leave?
search_queries: Do I pay the SEVIS I-901 fee again after a long leave?
records.answer:
**It depends on how long you were away and how your SEVIS record was handled.**

**You must get a new I-20/DS-2019 and pay the SEVIS I-901 fee again if:**
- You haven't been enrolled for **more than five (5) months**, or
- Your SEVIS record was terminated for any reason other than "Authorized Early Withdrawal."

In that case:
- Email ISSS **at least three (3) months** before your planned return for application instructions.
- This counts as a break in F-1 status. After you return, you must complete **at least one academic year of full-time study** before you're eligible for benefits like CPT or OPT.

**You may not need a new I-20 if:**
Your absence was authorized by ISSS and your break is **less than five months**. Then you can request a SEVIS reactivation instead. Submit these **1–2 months** before your return:
- I-94 Travel History (proof you left the U.S.)
- Flight itinerary showing your planned re-entry date
- Proof of full-time enrollment for the upcoming term

The page doesn't mention repaying the fee for a reactivation. However, SEVP decides each request. If SEVP denies it, you'll need a new I-20 instead.

**In all cases,** first get approval to return from your academic program and contact your academic advisor.

Source: [Vacation and Leave of Absence](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/vacation-loa). records.question: 212(e) two-year home country requirement
search_queries: 212(e) two-year home country requirement
records.answer:
# 212(e): Two-Year Home-Country Physical Presence Requirement

Some J-1 exchange visitors must live in their country of nationality or last legal permanent residence for a **total of two years** after leaving the U.S. Until then, they can't get U.S. permanent residency or change to another visa status inside the U.S.

**Who it applies to**
- Your J-1 program was funded, in whole or in part, by the U.S. government or your home government.
- Your field is on your home country's skills list, as designated by the U.S. Department of State.

**Effect on H-1B**
If you're subject to 212(e), you can't begin H-1B employment until you receive a 212(e) waiver. The H-1B FAQ says this waiver comes from USCIS.

**Waivers**
- **ISSS cannot help with J-1 waivers.** The Department of State considers this a conflict of interest for J-1 program sponsors.
- ISSS points to the Department of State for instructions (external): [Waiver of the Exchange Visitor Requirement](https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/us-visas/study/exchange/waiver-of-the-exchange-visitor.html).
- Processing can take a year or longer.
- A waiver application does not extend your legal stay.

records.answer:
**H-1B cap-gap** is the period between the end of your OPT (or STEM OPT) and the start of your H-1B status. If you qualify, your OPT work authorization is automatically extended while your change-of-status petition is pending.

**Eligibility**
- Your employer files an H-1B petition on or after April 1 requesting a change of status starting October 1.
- You're still within your OPT/STEM OPT period when the petition is filed.

**How long it lasts:** The ISSS OPT pages still say the extension runs through **October 1**. However, a newer ISSS announcement (January 16, 2025) says the H-1B Modernization Rule extends cap-gap **as late as April 1 of the following year**. Because today is past October 1 and these sources differ, please confirm your end date with ISSS. If your petition is still pending, ISSS also suggests consulting your H-1B immigration attorney.

**To get a cap-gap I-20, email ISSS:**
1. Confirm your employment and address are current. Inaccurate information delays the I-20.
2. Send one of these:
   - **Through June 1:** an employer statement that the petition was properly filed, plus proof of delivery to USCIS.
   - **Beyond June 1:** your USCIS receipt or proof that the petition was wait-listed.

**Keep in mind**
- If the petition is denied and your EAD has expired, your work permission ends on the denial date.
- The 90-day unemployment limit still applies during cap-gap.

records.question: What about during summer break?

What about during summer break? | How many hours can I work on campus?
records.answer:
**It depends on whether summer is your approved vacation term.** Immigration rules allow F-1 and J-1 students to work **more than 20 hours per week on campus during an approved vacation term**. The Office of Human Resources has its own (non-immigration) policies for working during that time, so check with them too.

**When summer counts as a vacation term:**
- You get **one vacation term per year**.
- **Quarter system:** after completing three consecutive quarters.
- **Semester system:** after completing two consecutive semesters.
- You're expected to enroll full-time again after the vacation term ends.

**If summer is not your vacation term** (for example, you're taking classes as a regular term or you're in a co-op cycle), the **20 hours per week** limit still applies.

The other conditions still apply. You must be maintaining valid status, you must not have graduated, and your I-20/DS-2019 must not have expired. J-1 students need prior ISSS authorization.

If you're unsure whether your summer counts as an approved vacation term, confirm with an ISSS advisor before working extra hours.

records.question: Can I travel abroad while it's pending?

Can I travel abroad while it's pending? | How long does it take USCIS to approve it? | What is OPT?
records.answer:
**It depends on where you are in your studies:**

- **Pre-Completion OPT:** You can travel and re-enter under the general F-1 travel requirements.
- **Post-Completion OPT, before you graduate:** If you're returning to continue your studies, the general F-1 travel requirements apply.
- **After graduation (during your 60-day grace period):** ISSS says travel is **"slightly risky."** The F-1 regulations don't directly address this situation, but most students have re-entered successfully with their USCIS OPT Receipt Notice.

**If you travel after graduating, carry:**
- A valid passport
- A valid F-1 visa (citizens of Canada and Bermuda are exempt)
- Your I-20 with the OPT recommendation and a travel signature **no older than 6 months**
- Your OPT Receipt Notice, which is mailed 2–3 weeks after USCIS receives your application

**If you're from a travel-restricted country:** A January 2026 ISSS announcement said USCIS placed holds on pending OPT applications for nationals of certain countries. A newer June 2026 update exists, but I don't have its details. If this applies to you, talk to ISSS before traveling.

Because travel decisions affect your status, it's best to confirm your plans with an ISSS advisor.

records.question: What do I need to do before I come back?
history: I want to take a term off and go home next quarter.
search_queries: What do I need to do before returning from an international break term?
What do I need to do before I come back? | I want to take a term off and go home next quarter.
records.answer:
It depends on whether ISSS approves your break, so it's best to know which case you're in before you leave.

**If ISSS approves an international break term**
Your record stays active. Before you return, have:
- A passport valid at least 6 months beyond your return date
- A valid F-1/J-1 visa
- A travel signature on your I-20/DS-2019 that won't be more than six months old when you return ([Signature Request form](https://drexel.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_6KHlTvO1gmy8Sfs))
- Proof of full-time enrollment for the next term

**If you take a leave of absence instead (SEVIS terminated)**
1. Get approval from your academic program to return.
2. If ISSS authorized your absence and it lasts **under 5 months**, submit your I-94 travel history, flight itinerary, and proof of full-time enrollment **1–2 months before returning** to request SEVIS reactivation. SEVP decides whether to approve this.
3. If you're away **over 5 months**, or SEVP denies reactivation, email ISSS **at least 3 months ahead** to get a new I-20/DS-2019 and repay the SEVIS I-901 fee. You'd then need one academic year of full-time study before being eligible for CPT/OPT.

**Before you leave**
ISSS advises caution with international travel because policies can change with little notice. If you'll need a new visa, or you're from a travel-ban country, consult ISSS before departing.

Sources: [Vacation and Leave of Absence](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/vacation-loa), [Visa Renewal](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/visa-renewal), [Spring 2026 Travel Advisory](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2026/March/International-Travel-Advisory---Spring-2026)

records.question: Who is eligible for it?

Who is eligible for it? | What is Academic Training for J-1 students?
records.answer:
To be eligible for Academic Training at Drexel, a J-1 student must meet **all** of these requirements:

- **Drexel-issued DS-2019:** Your DS-2019 must come from Drexel University, not an outside agency such as Fulbright.
- **Study is your main purpose:** You must be in the U.S. primarily to study, not to do academic training.
- **Good academic standing**
- **Related to your major:** The training must be directly related to the major field of study listed on your DS-2019.
- **Approved before your program ends:** AT must be approved and listed on your DS-2019 before your program end date.
- **Timely start:** The training must start no later than 30 days after your program ends.

The time limits from my last answer also apply, such as 18 months for bachelor's and master's students and 36 months for PhD students. Non-degree students can't extend their DS-2019 beyond 24 months in total, including both study and AT.

If you're unsure whether a specific position counts as "directly related" to your major, an [ISSS advisor](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support) can review your situation.

records.question: Tôi được phép thất nghiệp bao nhiêu ngày?
history: Tôi đang làm OPT sau khi tốt nghiệp.
search_queries: OPT unemployment grace period limits
Tôi được phép thất nghiệp bao nhiêu ngày? | Tôi đang làm OPT sau khi tốt nghiệp.
records.answer:
**Tối đa 90 ngày thất nghiệp** trong toàn bộ thời gian 12 tháng Post-Completion OPT. Đây là giới hạn cộng dồn, không phải liên tục.

**Cách tính:**
- Mỗi ngày (kể cả cuối tuần) không có việc làm hợp lệ đều bị tính, bắt đầu từ ngày bắt đầu làm việc ghi trên thẻ EAD.
- Nếu sau này được gia hạn **STEM OPT 24 tháng**, bạn có thêm 60 ngày, **tổng cộng tối đa 150 ngày** cho cả hai giai đoạn.

**Nếu sắp hết 90 ngày**, bạn **phải** thực hiện một trong các việc sau **trước** ngày thất nghiệp cuối cùng:
- Nộp đơn học tiếp (chuyển trường được SEVP chứng nhận hoặc đổi bậc học);
- Rời khỏi Hoa Kỳ;
- Thực hiện biện pháp khác để duy trì tình trạng hợp pháp.

**Nếu vượt quá giới hạn:** bạn mất tư cách F-1, hồ sơ SEVIS có thể bị chấm dứt, và bạn **không được hưởng 60 ngày ân hạn** khi OPT kết thúc. Điều này cũng có thể ảnh hưởng đến các quyền lợi nhập cư sau này (như H-1B hoặc thẻ xanh).

Ngoài ra, hãy nhớ báo cáo việc làm qua SEVIS Portal và báo cho ISSS nếu bạn mất việc hoặc bị gián đoạn công việc.

Nếu bạn đang gần chạm giới hạn, hãy liên hệ [ISSS](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support) để được cố vấn cho trường hợp cụ thể.
